name: Dipeptide-2
lead: Dipeptide-2 is a cosmetic peptide made of the amino acids valine and tryptophan. It is used in under-eye products to reduce the look of puffiness and bags. Its manufacturer says it increases lymphatic circulation, helping fluid drain from the delicate eye area.[1]

It is one of three actives in Eyeliss, an ingredient complex that also contains hesperidin methyl chalcone and palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7, marketed as a combined approach to puffy eyes.[1] The manufacturer reports a 20-person study with a 3% concentration of the complex in which 70% of participants improved after 56 days.[1]

chain: Dipeptide signals to boost lymphatic circulation
Less fluid retained under the eye
angle.text: Eye creams containing dipeptide-2 are used to make the under-eye area look less swollen. The mechanism, as described by the manufacturer, is improved drainage of fluid that makes bags look pronounced.

paras: No independent studies found. The ingredient's manufacturer reports a small study of 20 volunteers using the Eyeliss complex at 3%, with improvement in 70% after 56 days; it tested the three-active complex rather than dipeptide-2 alone.[1]
Dipeptide-2 appears in the ingredient lists of eye serums and creams aimed at puffiness. Ingredient guides classify its function as skin conditioning.[1]

card.summary: A valine-tryptophan peptide in eye creams that is said to boost lymphatic drainage and reduce under-eye puffiness.
card.note: Evidence is a small manufacturer study of a three-ingredient complex.

quick.overview:
Dipeptide-2 is a two-amino-acid peptide added to under-eye products to make puffy eyes look flatter and more rested.

It is part of the Eyeliss complex alongside hesperidin methyl chalcone and palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7.
quick.mechanism: The manufacturer says it increases lymphatic circulation so fluid drains away from the eye area.
quick.risks: Used topically in cosmetics; the available evidence is a small manufacturer study of the full complex, and no independent trials were found.
